subject: physics
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Isotopes of an element have the same number of:
questions.explain: Isotopes share proton number (same element) but differ in neutron number.

questions.q: A graph of maximum kinetic energy of photoelectrons against frequency has a gradient equal to:
questions.explain: From KEmax = hf − φ, the gradient of KEmax against f is the Planck constant h.

questions.q: The specific charge of a particle is defined as its:
questions.explain: Specific charge is the ratio of charge to mass (C/kg).

questions.q: An electron has momentum 3.3 × 10⁻²⁴ kg m/s. Its de Broglie wavelength is (h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J s):
An absorption spectrum appears as dark lines on a continuous spectrum because atoms:
options: Absorb only photons whose energy matches a level transition
questions.explain: Atoms absorb only photons with energy matching an electron transition, removing those specific wavelengths from the continuous spectrum.

questions.q: A nucleus is represented as 235/92 U. How many neutrons does it contain?
questions.explain: Neutron number equals mass number minus proton number, 235 - 92 = 143.

questions.q: A meson is composed of:
questions.explain: Mesons consist of one quark and one antiquark.

questions.q: Which of the following is a lepton?
questions.explain: The muon is a fundamental lepton; protons, neutrons and pions are hadrons.

questions.q: The y-intercept of a maximum-KE-versus-frequency graph for the photoelectric effect equals:
questions.explain: From KEmax = hf − φ, the intercept on the KE axis is −φ (negative of the work function).

questions.q: Which particle has the greatest specific charge?
questions.explain: The electron has a tiny mass yet carries one elementary charge, giving it the largest charge-to-mass ratio.

questions.q: The strange quark carries a strangeness of:
questions.explain: By convention the strange quark has strangeness -1.

questions.q: Which statement about a particle and its antiparticle is correct?
questions.explain: Antiparticles have the same rest mass but opposite charge (and opposite other quantum numbers).

questions.q: If the speed of an electron is increased, its de Broglie wavelength:
questions.explain: Since λ = h/p and p = mv, increasing speed increases momentum and therefore decreases the wavelength.

questions.q: In any particle interaction, the baryon number must be:
questions.explain: Baryon number is conserved in all known interactions.

questions.q: In the photoelectric effect, increasing the intensity of light above the threshold frequency increases:
options: The number of electrons emitted per second
The maximum kinetic energy of emitted electrons
questions.explain: Higher intensity means more photons per second, so more electrons are emitted, but their maximum KE is unchanged.

questions.q: In the reaction p -> n + e+ + neutrino, which conservation law confirms a neutrino (not antineutrino) appears?
questions.explain: The positron has lepton number -1, so a neutrino (+1) must be emitted to conserve lepton number.

questions.q: The minimum photon energy needed to produce an electron-positron pair is closest to:
questions.explain: Each particle has rest energy 0.511 MeV, so the minimum is 2 x 0.511 = 1.02 MeV.

questions.q: A line emission spectrum consists of discrete coloured lines because:
options: Atomic electrons occupy only discrete energy levels
questions.explain: Discrete spectral lines arise because electrons occupy quantised energy levels, so only specific photon energies are emitted.

questions.q: The work function of a metal is the:
options: Kinetic energy of the fastest electron
Minimum energy needed to release an electron from the metal surface
questions.explain: The work function φ is the minimum energy required to liberate an electron from the metal's surface.

questions.q: Confirm the proton charge: uud gives a total charge of:
questions.explain: (+2/3) + (+2/3) + (-1/3) = +1, so the proton has charge +1e.

questions.q: Hadrons are particles that:
options: are fundamental and feel only the weak force
questions.explain: Hadrons are composed of quarks and so experience the strong interaction.

questions.q: Light below the threshold frequency, however intense, produces no photoelectrons. This is best explained because:
options: Each electron absorbs many photons at once
Intensity does not affect electron emission
Each electron interacts with a single photon whose energy is too small
questions.explain: One electron absorbs one photon; if that single photon's energy hf is below φ, no electron is emitted regardless of intensity.

questions.q: The ionisation energy of an atom is the energy needed to:
options: Excite an electron to the next level
Completely remove an electron from the atom in its ground state
questions.explain: Ionisation energy is the energy required to remove an electron entirely (to the n = ∞, zero-energy level) from a ground-state atom.

questions.q: Excitation of an atom refers to:
options: An electron moving to a higher energy level within the atom
questions.explain: Excitation is when an electron absorbs energy and moves to a higher (but still bound) energy level.

questions.q: How many photons of wavelength 600 nm are needed to deliver 1.0 J of energy? (E ≈ 3.3 × 10⁻¹⁹ J per photon)
questions.explain: Number = total energy / photon energy = 1.0 / 3.3×10⁻¹⁹ ≈ 3.0×10¹⁸ photons.

questions.q: The maximum kinetic energy of photoelectrons depends on:
options: The intensity of the incident light
The size of the metal plate
The frequency of the incident light
questions.explain: Max KE = hf − φ, so it depends on the frequency of the light, not the intensity.

questions.q: What is the energy of a photon of wavelength 500 nm? (h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J s, c = 3.0 × 10⁸ m/s)
The electron lepton number of an electron neutrino is:
questions.explain: The electron neutrino, like the electron, has electron lepton number +1.

questions.q: The photoelectric effect cannot be explained by the wave model of light mainly because the wave model predicts:
options: Instant emission at all frequencies given enough intensity
questions.explain: The wave model predicts any frequency could eventually free electrons with enough intensity/time, contradicting the observed threshold frequency.

questions.q: In an electron diffraction tube, increasing the accelerating voltage causes the diffraction rings to:
questions.explain: Higher voltage gives electrons greater momentum and shorter de Broglie wavelength, so the diffraction rings shrink.
